open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:`public_op:deliverer_service.read_token`
open_points.text: The token with the whitespace around it removed.
open_points.question: Must `read_token` remove only the six characters in `TOKEN_TRIM_CHARACTERS`, as A5 rule 2 requires, or all characters the implementation regards as whitespace?
options: Remove only ASCII space, tab, line feed, carriage return, vertical tab and form feed.
Apply the language or library's general whitespace trimming.

witness.initial: The token file contains a non-breaking space followed by 32 visible ASCII characters.
outcomes: The non-breaking space is retained, so the token contains a non-visible-ASCII character and the start fails under A5 rule 2.
General whitespace trimming removes the non-breaking space, so the token is accepted and the service starts.
witness.observer: The deployment sees whether the service starts listening.

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:`public_op:deliverer_service.load_config`
open_points.text: An unknown time zone or an invalid connections file ends the start.
open_points.question: When both the time zone and the connections file are invalid, is the connections file read before or after the time-zone failure is decided?
options: Validate the time zone first and do not read the connections file.
Call `load_connections` first, then validate the time zone.
open_points.default_guess: Validate the time zone before reading the connections file.

witness.initial: The run settings name an unknown time zone and a connections file whose read is observable by an audit hook.
outcomes: The start fails without opening the connections file.
The connections file is opened once before the start fails.
witness.observer: The deployment or host audit system sees the file access.

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:`public_op:deliverer_service.run_service`
open_points.text: then serves the surface on the loopback interface and the `port` of the run settings until it is stopped.
open_points.question: Which loopback address and address family must the server bind?
options: Bind IPv4 `127.0.0.1` only.
Bind IPv6 `::1` only.
Bind both IPv4 and IPv6 loopback addresses.

witness.initial: The reverse proxy connects only to `127.0.0.1` on the configured port.
events: The service binds a loopback address.
The reverse proxy attempts its connection.
outcomes: An IPv4-loopback binding accepts the connection.
An IPv6-only binding is still a loopback binding but the proxy cannot connect.
witness.observer: The reverse proxy and calling flow see whether the service is reachable.

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:`public_op:deliverer_service.run_service`
open_points.text: The exit status of the process: 0 when it is stopped by a signal after it has served, 1 when the start fails, without listening, and a status other than 0 when the web server fails after it has started listening.
open_points.question: What exact exit status must represent a web-server failure after listening, and may it also be 1?
options: Use 1 for every failure, including a failure after listening.
Reserve 1 for start failure and use a different fixed status for a post-listening server failure.
Propagate an implementation-dependent nonzero web-server status.

witness.initial: The service has started listening and its web server then fails.
witness.observer: The deployment sees a different process status.

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:`public_op:deliverer_service.run_service`
open_points.text: 0 when it is stopped by a signal after it has served
open_points.question: Which signals count as a normal stop, and does a signal received after listening but before any request has been answered produce status 0?
options: Treat the server's normal termination signals as a successful stop once listening begins.
Return 0 only after at least one request has been served.
Preserve the signal-derived process status.
open_points.default_guess: Return 0 for a graceful SIGTERM or SIGINT received any time after listening begins.

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:`public_op:deliverer_router.create_app`
open_points.text: The method and path of each route of the manifest.
open_points.question: What are the exact HTTP methods and paths for health, scan, delivery and mark? No manifest passage containing them is given.
options: Define four explicit method/path pairs in this state.
Rely on unstated backend or prototype defaults.
open_points.default_guess: Define explicit method/path pairs before implementation.

witness.initial: A calling flow is configured with one plausible path for the scan operation.
events: The calling flow sends a scan request.
outcomes: An implementation using that path invokes `scan_route`.
An implementation using another plausible path answers 404 or 405.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees whether the operation is reachable.

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:`public_op:deliverer_router.create_app`
open_points.text:
The HTTP surface with the health, scan, delivery and mark routes, each bound to its handler in
`module:deliverer_api`.
open_points.question: Which named handler is bound to each method/path, and what application state or arguments supply the token and `DeliveryContext` to it?
options: Bind `answer_health`, `scan_route`, `deliver_route` and `mark_route` by their corresponding names and place context and token in application state.
Construct closures that capture context and token.
Pass context and token through an explicit framework dependency mechanism.
open_points.default_guess: Bind the correspondingly named handlers and provide immutable context and token through application state.

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:`public_op:deliverer_router.create_app`
open_points.text:
Every other route passes the request to its handler in `module:deliverer_api`, which checks the
token, the project id and the form of its body when it has one, calls one operation of `module:photo_delivery` and
turns its refusal into an answer.
open_points.question: How must the handler receive the raw `Authorization` fields so that it can distinguish exactly one field from duplicate fields before examining identifiers or the body?
options: Pass the raw repeated header entries to the handler.
Have the router reject missing or duplicate fields before invoking the handler.
Let the framework merge duplicate fields and validate the merged value.
open_points.default_guess: Pass all raw `Authorization` field occurrences to the handler without parsing the identifiers or body.

witness.initial: A request carries two `Authorization` fields whose framework-combined value could resemble one credential.
outcomes: Raw multiplicity is preserved and the request is refused with `unauthorized`.
The framework merges or selects a value and the request can be accepted.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees 401 versus execution of the requested operation.

open_points.subject: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
open_points.question: State 3 makes `check_token`, `scan_route`, `deliver_route` and `mark_route` public capabilities imported by `deliverer_router`, but State 5 gives no public-operation contract for any of them. What are their callers, inputs, outputs, errors, effects and state impacts?
options: Add a State 5 public-operation unit for each of the four operations.
Make them private and change the router's public dependency surface and binding design.
open_points.default_guess: Add four explicit public-operation contracts owned by `deliverer_api`.

open_points.subject: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
open_points.question: What does `check_token` accept and return, how does it represent the one principal, and does it return or raise the `unauthorized` refusal for every missing, duplicate or malformed `Authorization` field?
options: Accept all raw header occurrences and return the authenticated principal or raise a `DelivererError` carrying `UNAUTHORIZED`.
Accept one already-extracted value and return a boolean.
Return an `AuthenticationRequired` value for failures.
open_points.default_guess: Accept raw header occurrences, return the single authenticated principal on success, and raise the fixed `UNAUTHORIZED` refusal on failure.

open_points.subject: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
open_points.question: What request values does `scan_route` accept, what exact success body and HTTP status does it return, and how does it map each `DelivererError` to M08?
options: Return a serialized `ScanResult` with status 200 and map refusals through `REFUSAL_STATUS` and `REFUSAL_DETAIL`.
Return only the observation list without counts.
Return framework-native response objects whose shape is left to the implementation.
open_points.default_guess: Return the complete serialized `ScanResult` with status 200 and fixed M08 mapping.

open_points.subject: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
open_points.question: What exact request parsing, success body, success status and refusal mapping belong to `deliver_route`, including malformed JSON, missing fields, extra fields and duplicate JSON member names?
options: Require one JSON object with exactly one string `name` and one string `source_id`, reject every other raw form as `INVALID_REQUEST`, and return M06 with status 200.
Validate only the parsed object, allowing the JSON parser's duplicate-member policy.
Let the web framework generate its own validation response.
open_points.default_guess: Define strict request parsing and return M06 with status 200; every form defect becomes the fixed `INVALID_REQUEST` M08.

open_points.subject: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
open_points.question: What exact request parsing, identifier validation, success body, success status and refusal mapping belong to `mark_route`?
options: Require the fixed publication request form, validate project id and `photo_id` before calling `photo_delivery`, return `MarkOutcome` with status 200, and use the fixed M08 mapping.
Return M07 alone and encode `MarkStatus` separately.
Allow framework-native validation errors.
open_points.default_guess: Return the complete `MarkOutcome` with status 200 after strict API-owned validation, and map all refusals through the fixed M08 tables.

open_points.subject: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
open_points.text: `AuthenticationRequired`, a request that does not carry the token.
open_points.question: What are the fields and semantics of `AuthenticationRequired`, and does it describe only a missing field or every authentication failure covered by A5 rule 1?
options: It is a raw request/header carrier used for all A5 rule 1 failures.
It is a marker representing only an absent credential.
Remove it because handlers inspect raw requests and refusals use M08.
open_points.default_guess: Remove the model unless the router backend requires a precisely defined raw-header carrier.

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:`public_op:deliverer_api.answer_health`
open_points.text: The health answer with the status `ok`.
open_points.question: What is the exact health response body and HTTP status exposed by the route?
options: Return `{"status":"ok"}` with HTTP 200.
Return the string `ok` with HTTP 200.
Return an empty HTTP 204 response while treating `ok` as internal state.

witness.initial: The service is listening and a deployment health probe expects a JSON object.
events: The probe calls the health route.
outcomes: The probe receives `{"status":"ok"}` and accepts the service.
The probe receives a string or empty body and rejects the service.
witness.observer: The deployment health probe sees the response representation.

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:`public_op:object_connections.load_connections`
open_points.text: An unreadable file, a file of another form or a subfolder that breaks the form of A5 rule 8 raises an error.
open_points.question: What exact JSON record form does `load_connections` accept, including the top-level shape, record keys, field types, treatment of unknown fields, duplicate project ids or JSON member names, and correspondence between a map key and M01 `project_id`?
options: Define a closed JSON schema and reject duplicates, unknown fields and key/field disagreement.
Allow extra fields and use the last duplicate value.
Accept either a keyed object or a list of M01 records.
open_points.default_guess: Define and enforce one closed JSON schema, reject all duplicates and unknown fields, and require the key to equal the canonical `project_id`.

witness.initial: The connections file contains two records for the same project with different confirmation values.
outcomes: A strict implementation rejects the whole file and the service does not listen.
A last-record-wins implementation accepts the file and starts with one of the connections.
witness.observer: The deployment sees whether the service starts, and later callers see which connection is used.

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis.md:`public_op:object_connections.load_connections`
open_points.question: Which error type and payload must `load_connections` raise, so `load_config` can distinguish the expected invalid-file failure from an implementation failure?
options: Raise `DelivererError` carrying `FOLDER_UNAVAILABLE`.
Raise a dedicated configuration or connections-file exception.
Propagate JSON, Unicode and operating-system exceptions directly.
open_points.default_guess: Raise one dedicated connections-file exception that `load_config` converts into start failure and `confirmed_connection` converts into `FOLDER_UNAVAILABLE`.
